title: Context-aware aggregation and attenuation for SLO alerting to reduce pager noise
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: After a series of capacity regressions and two recent SLO breaches, oncall teams reported high pager churn driven by short-lived burn spikes and late-stage degradation signals. This ticket implements a context-aware aggregation and attenuation strategy to reduce actionable alerts while preserving detection for real incidents.

Goals:
- Reduce P1 pager frequency from transient burn spikes by >=60% in non-customer-facing tiers.
- Maintain time-to-detect for sustained SLO breaches within current SLO targets (no more than +1m median).
- Add signal context (region, capacity mode, affected model) to every alert payload to enable better routing.

Scope:
- Introduce sliding 'contextual burn windows' that adapt burn-rate evaluation based on recent capacity changes and request burst patterns.
- Implement aggregation logic to group correlated burn alerts across zones/instances and emit a single summary alert.
- Add attenuation rules: short-lived spikes (under threshold length) are logged and moved to a non-paging channel unless they co-occur with error-rate regressions.
- Tag alerts with routing metadata (customer tier, dedicated/private flag) so oncall routing can filter lower-tier noise when appropriate.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New aggregation reduces duplicate alerts for same root cause by >50% in staging over a 72h test.
2) Paging only occurs for aggregated incidents with sustained burn or associated error signals.
3) Alert payload includes keys: region, model_family, capacity_mode, customer_tier, burst_score.
4) Runbook updated and verified; oncall walkthrough completed and acknowledged by SRE and Platform teams.

Out of scope: changing SLO definitions, major rewrites to alerting backend (we will add as layered rules on top of existing burn-rate service).
tasks: Design contextual burn window algorithm (Aisha + ML infra)
Prototype aggregation service that deduplicates alerts across zones (Diego)
Add attenuation policy engine with configurable thresholds per customer_tier
Create a non-paging observability channel and retention policy for short spikes
Update runbooks and perform oncall tabletop exercise
Deploy to staging for 72h validation and collect metrics
implementation_notes:
Prototype will sit as a thin layer between burn-rate detector and PagerDuty integration. It will subscribe to the burn-rate event stream, apply a time-decay aggregation window keyed by (model_family, region, capacity_mode, customer_tier), compute a burst_score, and decide: page / log-only / non-paging notification. Use existing attribution IDs to link back to traces. Keep the initial rollout as a feature flag per cluster.

Important trade-offs discussed: Longer aggregation windows reduce noise but increase detection latency; we will start with adaptive windows bounded [30s, 5m] and tune based on staging feedback. We will not suppress alerts that coincide with error-rate or request-failure signals.

Data retention for logged, non-paging incidents: 30 days in AlertsArchive. Aggregated alert ids must map to original detector events for debugging.

test_plan: Replay recent capacity event traces into staging to measure duplicate suppression and false-suppression rate
Run 72h live validation on stg-eu-2 with feature flag enabled; compare paging volume vs baseline
Simulate combined burn + error regressions to confirm no suppression when errors present
Oncall walkthrough and sign-off after 72h window
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased detection latency. Mitigation: Hard upper bound on aggregation window and progressive rollout via feature flag.
Risk: Suppressing real incidents during correlated failures. Mitigation: Require co-occurrence of error-rate signals to allow suppression; immediate un-suppression if error signals spike.
Risk: Missing customer-impacting events for dedicated/private customers. Mitigation: Per-tier attenuation thresholds and explicit tagging to bypass suppression for high-tier customers.
